heroHeadline: Day 30: Bamako Siege Crosses One-Month Mark on Eid al-Adha; Post-Truce Period Begins; Al-Shabaab Congratulates JNIM Globally
heroSubtitle: Day 30 of JNIM's declared 'total siege' of Bamako (announced April 28, 2026) as of May 28, 2026 — the one-month mark. Eid al-Adha begins today, marking the formal expiry of the March 2026 fuel-corridor truce under which Mali released 100+ jihadist detainees in exchange for JNIM opening fuel supplies. JNIM now faces no truce obligation and retains structural road-junction control to reinstate total blockade at will. AP reporting published May 28 documented that sheep traders who normally bring 200 animals to Bamako for Eid brought only 50 this year; small sheep that cost ~$177 normally now cost ~$266. Al-Shabaab spokesman Ali Mohamed Rage publicly congratulated JNIM in a global Eid address documented by the Long War Journal — an unprecedented inter-affiliate solidarity signal at the height of the Bamako crisis. Three key ongoing fronts: (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE (Day 30): 3 of 6 supply roads cut (Amnesty International, May 15); WFP suspended ($620M gap, 2M affected); IRC emergency response active; FAO projects 52.8M at acute food insecurity IPC Phase 3+ for June–August lean season. Bamako food and livestock prices remain +43–100% above pre-siege baselines. Manantali power grid degraded. US Embassy security alert active through May 31. (2) KIDAL AERIAL CAMPAIGN (ongoing): FAMa/Africa Corps continue striking FLA/JNIM-held Kidal with Su-type fighters and armed drones; no ground-offensive capacity confirmed. Africa Corps operates from Anéfis and Gao. (3) INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY: FIDH/TRIAL International/PALU African Court case (filed April 20) proceeds; Goubré IDP camp massacre (80 killed May 22) and cluster bomb allegations (Tadjmart, RFI-confirmed RBK-500/ShOAB-0.5) sustain IHL documentation pressure. No ceasefire negotiations reported. Post-Eid window (May 28–June 5) is the highest-risk period since the siege began.
